title: Optional read-only HSDA-style API endpoint over the published dataset
context: The default distribution is static HSDS JSON/CSV/GeoJSON files (a read-only static API). If a downstream reuser (211/AIRS system, civic app, community map) needs a live queryable endpoint, an optional HSDA-style read-only API can be added as a thin layer over the published dataset. This is backlog — activate only if a reuser specifically needs it and the static exports are insufficient. The API must be read-only, serve no recipient data, and add no telemetry.
objective: Implement an optional, read-only HSDA-compatible API endpoint over the published food-assistance-maps dataset. The API must: (1) serve only the published (verified, freshness-gated) entries; (2) support basic HSDA query parameters (location, service_type, status); (3) be read-only with no write endpoints; (4) add no telemetry or tracker; (5) include correct CORS headers for cross-origin civic-tech use; and (6) be deployable as a serverless function or edge worker over the static dataset.
acceptanceCriteria: API exposes read-only HSDA-compatible endpoints for listing and filtering services (by location, service_type, operating_status)
No write, update, or delete endpoints exist
API serves only published (verified, freshness-gated) entries — the same set as the static exports
No recipient/client data fields are returned by any endpoint
No telemetry or tracker is introduced by the API layer
CORS headers are set correctly to allow cross-origin requests from civic-tech consumers
API is documented (OpenAPI spec or equivalent) with field descriptions and example responses
API activation is gated on a confirmed downstream reuser who needs it (static exports were insufficient for their use case)
output: src/api/ (HSDA-style API implementation) + docs/api.md (API documentation / OpenAPI spec), deployable as a serverless function.
